children: Dalian iron ore futures fell on Thursday, as rising shipments and deepening losses at steel mills weighed on prices.
The most-traded January iron ore contract on China's Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE)
closed daytime trade 0.28% lower at 711.5 yuan ($105.96) a metric ton.
The benchmark October iron ore <SZZFV6> on the Singapore Exchange was 0.1% higher at $95.85 a ton.

Supply remained abundant, with shipments from top producer Australia climbing above 21 million tons week-on-week, contributing to elevated port arrivals, despite some volatility, said analysts from Everbright Futures in a note.
Iron ore inventories at seven major ports in Australia and Brazil rose 258,000 tons to 11.95 million tons in the week to September 20, rebounding slightly, data from consultancy Mysteel showed.

The average cost of molten iron and steel billets at mainstream mills in Tangshan rose slightly this week, with mill losses continuing to widen based on an ex-factory standard square billet price of 3,010 yuan a ton on September 23, Mysteel data showed.

Molten iron output recovered slightly to 2.38 million tons on September 23, driven mainly by pre-holiday restocking, though additional furnace maintenance is limiting room for further gains, said analysts from consultancy Mysteel in a note.
Mills are now nearing the end of that restocking cycle, which could cause demand to ease slightly, they added.
Other steelmaking ingredients on the DCE fell, with coking coal
Steel benchmarks on the Shanghai Futures Exchange were weaker. Rebar
